textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 science · Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: In a physical change no new substance is formed. Melting ice, dissolving sugar, cutting paper and stretching a rubber band are physical changes. Many physical changes can be reversed.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: In a physical change no new substance is formed. Melting ice, dissolving sugar, cutting paper and stretching a rubber band are physical changes. Many physical changes can be reversed.
beats.speakEn: In a physical change no new substance is formed. Melting ice, dissolving sugar, cutting paper and stretching a rubber band are physical changes. Many physical changes can be reversed.

beats.en: In a chemical change a new substance is formed with different properties. Burning wood, rusting iron, cooking food and souring milk are chemical changes.
beats.speakEn: In a chemical change a new substance is formed with different properties. Burning wood, rusting iron, cooking food and souring milk are chemical changes.

type: Key Concept: In a physical change no new substance is formed.
Rule: In a chemical change a new substance is formed with different properties.

textbookBox.concept: Rusting needs iron, air and water. We prevent it by painting, oiling or galvanising. Combustion needs fuel, a source of oxygen in common examples, and enough heat for the reaction.

beats.en: Salt can form crystals when some water evaporates from a concentrated salt solution. The solid crystals are the same salt that was dissolved.

textbookBox.concept: Cooking can be useful, while rusting can damage tools. Changes can also take different amounts of time. A fruit can ripen slowly and a pencil can snap quickly.
